chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him about the al-Anfal (spoils of war/land revenue), so he said: 'Every barren land or anything that belonged to the kings is exclusively for the Imam, with no share for the people.' And he said: 'Among them are the two seas (Bahrain), upon which no expedition was made with horses or camels.'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: Al-Anfal (spoils of war or land revenue)
key_terms.الْبَحْرَانِ: The two seas (referring to the region of Bahrain)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Al-Anfal and who owns it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between *Anfal* (booty) and *Ghanimah* (spoils of war), establishing that properties of the kings and barren lands are exclusively the Imam’s domain. It specifically cites Bahrain as a prime example of territory acquired through *Khums* rather than active combat, highlighting the theological principle that the Imam’s authority extends over these resources for the benefit of the community.
